title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: applicant conditions — profile age, misdeclaration block and waiting period after a rejection
content:
## Rule
An application under the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product is admitted only when the applicant meets three conditions, each established from the line's records before the application is registered:
1. **Profile age.** The applicant's profile must be at least the category's minimum profile age, in calendar days, old on the application date. The record relied on is the date on which the customer profile was opened.
2. **No recent misdeclaration.** The applicant must have no misdeclaration penalty inside the category's misdeclaration block, in calendar days, before the application.
3. **Waiting period after a rejection.** A new application for a booking whose previous application was rejected is accepted only from the category's waiting period, in calendar days, after the previous application was rejected. The earliest date is the previous application's rejection date plus the category's waiting days, counted on calendar dates, and an application on that earliest date is accepted.

## How the misdeclaration block is counted
- The window is the trailing run of calendar days ending on the handling date, of the length of the misdeclaration block of the category applied for.
- The count covers misdeclaration penalty charges booked against the customer, on any of its acceptances, with a charge date inside that window.
- An inspection cost recovery charge is not a misdeclaration penalty for this count.
- The condition is met only when that count is zero.

## Waiting period — boundary cases (hypothetical 3-day waiting period)
| Previous application rejected on | Earliest accepted date | New application dated | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 May | 13 May | 12 May | not accepted |
| 10 May | 13 May | 13 May | accepted |
| 10 May | 13 May | 15 May | accepted |

The rejection date that starts the clock is the one recorded on the previous application for the same booking.

## Profile age — boundary cases (hypothetical 60-day minimum)
- Profile opened 1 March, application dated 30 April: the profile is 60 days old, which is at least 60 — the condition is met.
- Profile opened 1 March, application dated 29 April: the profile is 59 days old — the condition is not met.

## Points of judgement
- *Does the customer's assurance that it has never misdeclared settle condition 2?* No; the count is taken from the misdeclaration penalty charges on the line's records.
- *Does the waiting period apply to an application on a different booking?* The condition is stated for a new application for the booking whose previous application was rejected.
